summary.headline: Concord Enviro FY26 revenue fell 6.2% to INR557.8 crores and EBITDA dropped 57.9% to INR36.6 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin was 9%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR206 crores, flat YoY and up 65% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR18.5 crores (9% margin) against 27.7% a year earlier. Management attributed the shortfall to the delayed Kenya project, deferred CBG revenues, and Sharjah supply disruptions from Middle East tensions, which caused missed March deliveries of about INR43 crores. Order book stands at INR536 crores for FY27 execution (INR828 crores total signed value including long-term O&M), with L1 status on ZLD orders worth INR143 crores not yet awarded. Management declined to give firm FY27 revenue or margin guidance until Q1 results, citing the Middle East conflict.

financial_highlights.change: vs net loss of INR8.1 crores in Q3 FY26 and profit of INR47.1 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Water / wastewater (S&P: sale of plants, supply and projects)
segments.commentary: Sale of plants including water and CBG accounted for about INR334 crores of order book at 31 March 2026. Management said S&P share was high in Q4, which pressured gross margin.

segments.name: Consumables and spares
segments.commentary: Consumables and spares order book about INR41.5 crores as of 31 March 2026.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Annual O&M order book about INR160 crores for FY27. Largest O&M contract in company history at INR80 crores; Fatek Utilities acquired. A 10-year O&M contract was also signed with a leading EPC company.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas)
segments.commentary: CBG order book about INR20-odd crores. Projects moved into execution but revenue slipped to FY27 on financial closure delays and feedstock availability.

segments.name: ZLD (zero liquid discharge) / steel
segments.commentary: L1 on ZLD orders worth INR143 crores, including an order above INR100 crores from a large Indian steel maker; award letter awaited. First waste pickle liquor ZLD system developed.

segments.name: H-Xtreme Heat Exchanger
segments.commentary: Newly launched product with 10-25% fuel savings and up to 90% efficiency. Targets a USD40 million market; first order not yet received, expected in May 2026. Management targets double-digit share within 3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of about INR1,000 crores: India S&P INR350-400 crores, exports INR200-250 crores, desalination and naval INR150-200 crores, large EPC-type CETP and corporate projects about INR300 crores.
EBITDA target of 14-16% remains unchanged on paper, but management warned that rising raw material prices, air freight use and cost pressures could cause dips; detailed impact to be given in Q1 FY27.
Q1 FY27 expected to remain somewhat depressed due to conflict-related delivery slowness; management expects revenue and margin recovery from Q2 FY27, aided by contracts signed in May.
Kenya project to proceed in phases, with first phase expected to start in July 2026 and visibility improving in Q2 FY27.
Nuclear-related order at Visakhapatnam (INR36 crores excluding taxes) to execute across Q2-Q4 FY27 with commissioning targeted for Q4 FY27.
Management declined to give FY27 or FY28 revenue guidance until Q1 results.
capex_capacity: Investment of USD 2 million in a minority equity stake in a US-based polymer company, the second US investment after an earlier membrane technology company stake.
INR93 crores investment in FY26 cited by an analyst; CFO said it lands on the balance sheet as investment in businesses (Nala Membranes) and not in mutual funds.
Fatek Utilities Private Limited acquired to strengthen O&M business.
Raw effluent membrane technology completed pilot field trials; ZLD system for steel developed.
Teams strengthened in employee costs to support H-Xtreme, CBG and other new products, creating accumulated cost on balance sheet until revenues scale.
Sharjah manufacturing operations disrupted; shipments routed via Khor Fakkan port due to Jebel Ali volumes being low and congestion at Khor Fakkan.
demand_pricing: Order book (signed value) INR828 crores total including long-term O&M; INR536 crores is the portion to be delivered in FY27.
Q1 FY27 order intake target about 60-65% already converted, per management, with several large orders expected to be finalised.

Metals and mining (including steel) cited as the largest big-ticket opportunity; solar PV manufacturing pipeline strengthening with advanced talks; textile, pharma and chemicals active in smaller orders.
Smaller orders (below INR5 crores) described as bread-and-butter business for chemical, pharma and textile clients; large orders are mostly equipment-supply heavy with reduced civil component.
Management acknowledged more competition on larger projects.
CBG: feedstock scarcity and rising feedstock prices are a challenge for existing plants; company focusing on on-site industrial organic waste feedstock.
Diageo: Uganda orders largely executed; Kenya delayed, with the client sold to another brewer after change of control.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and EBITDA margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a strong order book but declined to give numbers, citing the Middle East conflict and Sharjah disruption; more colour promised in Q1 results. Target EBITDA margin of 14-16% unchanged, subject to cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher share of S&P projects, lower export mix, BOT projects completed in the year, missed membrane shipments from Dubai, and rising costs; said margins should be maintained barring conflict impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the order book been flat and are costs uncompetitive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some March orders were pushed into Q1 by clients, not lost; around 60-65% of the Q1 intake target is already converted, and no change in order-win outlook was seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total order book and does it include the steel order?
qa_highlights.answer: Signed order value is INR828 crores including long-term O&M; INR536 crores is FY27 execution. The INR143 crore ZLD L1 steel order is not yet included as the award letter is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Has the heat exchanger generated its first order?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; the first order is expected in May 2026. Several trial plants have been placed with chemical clients, and the target is double-digit share of a USD40 million market within three years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 order inflow targets by sector?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR1,000 crores: India S&P INR350-400 crores, exports INR200-250 crores, desalination and naval INR150-200 crores, and EPC-type CETP and corporate projects about INR300 crores.

risks_watch: Sharjah supply chain and Khor Fakkan port congestion; Q1 FY27 deliveries may stay slow.
Award timing of the INR143 crore ZLD (steel) L1 order and conversion of Q1 order pipeline.
Rising raw material and air freight costs versus the 14-16% EBITDA margin target; Q1 to quantify the impact.
Kenya project phasing and Diageo next-phase investment, which management expects clarity on after July 2026.
CBG feedstock scarcity, digester performance and financial closure delays.
Working capital intensity of large projects; management said each project is financed and managed separately.
Q4 FY26 revenue shortfall of about INR43 crores attributed to deferred deliveries.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term execution and reluctant to give numerical guidance until Q1 FY27, citing the Middle East conflict. Confident on the order book, pipeline and long-term growth drivers such as H-Xtreme, solar PV and O&M.
